description: Pool of voice IDs used by action, system, tutorial, sequencer and character-specific controllers when one spoken line is selected for a named event.

Id.technical: FName primary key (export field ID). Producers select group IDs from CharacterVoiceGroup.Id_VoiceGroup, ShikigamiVoiceGroup.Id_VoiceGroup, CharacterSound.Id_VoiceGroup (index GroupKind - 1), hard-coded tutorial TaskTextIds and CP_240's CN_210_IDLE literal, sequencer random-section IDs/AllyGroupVoiceSetId, and generated <character>_APPEARANCE_0n / _VICTORY_0n names in the unique-pair evaluator. DTM.VoiceGroupDataTables (+0x750) is resolved from the DataTable primary asset named VoiceGroupDataTable. The shared typed finder and direct FindRow loops return the first matching typed row in table order; None IDs are rejected (ActionController_FindVoiceGroupRow skips None even when bCheckNone is false, and direct consumers that take external IDs test IsNone).

Id_Voice.simple: Voice IDs in the random-pick pool.
Id_Voice.technical: TArray<FName>; no weights, timers or per-entry metadata are stored. None is the unused-slot sentinel: all 5,464 exported rows have five entries and every row has at least one non-None voice, although four rows have an interior None rather than only trailing placeholders. Sound voice player synthesizes weight 1 per non-None entry and 0 per None and picks a weighted index; battle tutorial shuffles non-None original indices after excluding the caller's Exclude index and, for TextIndex 0, StepTarget; generic character action and CP_240 compact non-None candidates and remove a cached previous pick only when at least two remain; shikigami counts non-None entries but indexes the original array, so an interior None can be selected; sequencer random 2D/3D compacts None and uses the sequence random stream; unique-pair common fallback collects non-None IDs and chooses deterministically with ComputeSideSeed(Side) % Num. The chosen ID is ultimately resolved in DTM.VoiceDataTables (+0x740) to cue-sheet/cue rows.

notes: Loaded as a 'DataTable' primary asset named VoiceGroupDataTable into DTM.VoiceGroupDataTables (+0x750); consumers either walk that array or use a typed first-match finder, with the first matching table winning.
This is the second layer of the usual voice join: action/system data selects a VoiceGroup row, and one of this array's entries selects a VoiceDataTable row to play.

Runtime gates decide whether a group is consulted: character and shikigami action voice require both bActionVoiceEnabled and bVoiceGroupPlaybackEnabled; tutorial task voice returns while voice slot 0 is playing; CP_240 variant playback is limited to the player's character and a free Voice3D slot; sequencer random evaluators require enabled sections and resolved actors.

None placeholders are common and are normally filtered. The shikigami consumer counts non-None entries but then indexes the original array with the fraction of that count, so a None entry in the middle could still be selected; this is an observed implementation quirk, not a data rule.

The combined export has 5,464 uniquely keyed rows and is exactly partitioned across the 47 datatables_by_character VoiceGroup shards, with no row differences. Join checks find all 700 CharacterSound.Id_VoiceGroup references and all 47 ShikigamiVoiceGroup references present, but 10 CharacterVoiceGroup.Id_VoiceGroup references point to absent group rows and 40 exported Id_Voice candidates are absent from the VoiceDataTable export; these are export/reference observations, not proof of runtime behavior.

The export and reconstructed C++ do not establish retail row completeness or Blueprint-only consumers. Source is reconstructed retail C++ with retail RVAs recorded inline; no retail Blueprint evidence was available.

usages.detail: Shared typed voice-group row finder used by action and sequencer lookups.
Action controller selects a group ID from the CharacterVoiceGroup row, with Index/Index-1/GetAttackVoiceIndex cases and unchecked array access.
Resolves the selected VoiceGroup row, compacts non-None candidates and removes the cached prior voice when at least two remain.
CharacterSound voice group path uses a uniform weighted lottery over non-None entries.
Battle tutorial task voice shuffles non-None candidates and avoids the excluded index and prior first-text line.
CP_240 removes the last picked variant before a studio-stream random selection.
Shikigami voice group random pick with the original-array index quirk.
2D sequencer random voice selects the ally group or section ID and uses the sequence random stream.
3D sequencer random voice uses the same group precedence for bound actors.
Unique-pair common fallback resolves generated appearance/result group IDs and collects non-None voices for deterministic side-seed selection.
